item.title: Spatially varying modified Chaplygin gas wormhole with minimum violation of energy condition
item.description: arXiv:2611.28130v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this study, we explore the existence of traversable wormhole solutions in general relativity using a power-law shape function given by $b(r) = r^{\alpha}$. Departing from the conventional approach--where matter content is derived a posteriori from the field equations--we instead prescribe a generalized, radially dependent equation of state: $p(r) = \omega_1(r)\rho(r) - \frac{\omega_2(r)}{\rho(r)^{\gamma}}$. This formulation smoothly transitions from a Chaplygin-like behavior at small radii to a linear barotropic regime at large distances. We obtain an analytical expression for the energy density and derive the radial pressure in closed form. The redshift function is derived using the field equation and the equation of state. Ultimately, we demonstrate that this spatially varying modified Chaplygin gas equation of state successfully confines the exotic matter to the immediate vicinity of the throat. Moreover, we demonstrate that the requirement of consistency between the prescribed equation of state and the Einstein field equations fixes the throat value of the second coefficient, $B =\alpha$, thereby removing the apparent indeterminacy in the redshift function near the throat. For the specific choices $\omega_1(r) = \left(1 - r^{-m}\right)\omega_\infty$ and $\omega_2(r) = B\, r^{-k}$, with the decay condition $k > \gamma(3-\alpha)$, the non-linear term is suppressed at spatial infinity and the model reduces to a barotropic fluid with $p \simeq \omega_\infty \rho$, yielding an asymptotically well-behaved geometry. Our results indicate that the choice of the equation of state is not a mere mathematical convenience but a fundamental ingredient that controls both the localization of exotic matter and the asymptotic viability of the wormhole solution.
item.dc:creator: Sara Rastgoo, Foad Parsaei

item.title: Observational Aspects of Black Holes in Square-Root Electrodynamic Backgrounds
item.description: arXiv:2611.28145v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by recent thermodynamic investigations \cite{nn}, we study the optical behaviors of black holes in a square-root nonlinear electrodynamic framework. More precisely, we examine the shadow aspect of black holes obtained by considering the electrodynamic Lagrangian $\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{F})=\mathcal{F} \sqrt{1-k(2Q^2\mathcal{F})^{1/4}},$ where $\mathcal{F}$ is the Maxwell gauge invariant, $k$ is a relevant dimensionless parameter, and $Q$ is considered as a magnetic charge. By confronting the obtained results with the Event Horizon Telescope collaboration findings, we provide the corroborated moduli space regions. Then, we approach such optical behaviors using machine learning techniques. As a result, we observe a possible compatibility with the Sgr $A^*_{Keck}$ black hole model.
item.dc:creator: Maryem Jemri

item.title: Mathematical basis, phase transitions and singularities of (3+1)-dimensional phi4 scalar field model
item.description: arXiv:2511.07439v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The lambda phi4 scalar field model can be applied to interpret pion-pion scattering and properties of hadrons. In this work, the mathematical basis, phase transitions and singularities of a (3+1)-dimensional (i.e., (3+1)D) phi4 scalar field model are investigated. It is found that as a specific example of topological quantum field theories, the (3+1)D phi4 scalar field model must be set up on the Jordan-von Neumann-Wigner framework and dealt with the parameter space of complex time (or complex temperature). The use of the time average and the topologic Lorentz transformation representing Reidemeister moves ensure the integrability, which takes into account for the contributions of nontrivial topological structures to physical properties of the many-body interacting system. The ergodic hypothesis is violated at finite temperatures in the (3+1)D phi4 scalar field model. Because the quantum field theories with ultraviolet cutoff can be mapped to the models in statistical mechanics, the (3+1)D phi4 scalar field model with ultraviolet cutoff is studied by inspecting its relation with the three-dimensional (3D) Ising model. Furthermore, the direct relation between the coupling K in the 3D Ising model and the bare coupling lambda0 in the (3+1)D phi4 scalar field model is determined in the strong coupling limit. The results obtained in the present work can be utilized to investigate thermodynamic physical properties and critical phenomena of quantum (scalar) field theories.
item.dc:creator: Zhidong Zhang

item.title: Solar System and Atomic Clock Bounds on Locally Coupled Swampland Scalars
item.description: arXiv:2606.27388v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study how local measurements constrain light scalar fields that are relevant in late time cosmic acceleration and are often discussed in connection with swampland criteria. Starting from a scalar-tensor framework, we define the swampland slope and curvature variables in the canonically normalized Einstein frame and relate them to Solar System tracking, Lunar Laser Ranging, equivalence principle tests and atomic clock comparisons. These measurements do not constrain the scalar velocity by itself, but products of that velocity with microscopic couplings to matter, gravity and atomic parameters. For coupling directions visible to local experiments, the scalar is driven into an ultra slow present regime. This severely restricts the possibility of realizing an $\mathcal{O}(1)$ de Sitter gradient through unscreened visible sector couplings alone. The refined de Sitter alternative remains possible, but in the single field hilltop realization it requires proximity to the maximum or a tuned suppression of the growing mode.
item.dc:creator: Suraj Gavhale, Maxim Khlopov, Oem Trivedi, Maxim Krasnov

item.title: Jordan-Frame Dynamics of Curvature Inflation: A Derivative Expansion of the Friedmann Constraint
item.description: arXiv:2611.21662v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We derive a slow-roll approximation for the Jordan-frame Hubble rate $H_J$ in metric $f(R)$ gravity. A derivative expansion of the vacuum Friedmann constraint to third order gives $\dot H_J$ as a function of $H_J$. In the Starobinsky model we also show that the difference in $\dot H_J$ between two expanding solutions decreases as they pass through successively lower values of $H_J$, and that a signed square root of $H_J$ evolves smoothly through the zeros that follow inflation. We test the approximation in a regularized inverse-logarithmic $R^2$ model and in $R+\alpha^{p-1}R^p$, taking the pivot from the exact background 60 Einstein-frame e-folds before the end of inflation. For the inverse-logarithmic coupling $\delta=3$, the third-order approximation reproduces $\dot H_J$ at the pivot with a relative error of $3\times10^{-8}$. Integrating the approximate branch between the pivot and exit values of $H_J$ taken from the exact background gives 59.98 e-folds, compared with 60 on the exact trajectory. At the six couplings $\delta=0,1,\ldots,5$, the absolute difference from the numerical mode result is below $1.1\times10^{-5}$ in the scalar tilt $n_s$, and the relative difference is below $0.0052\%$ in the tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$. Here the second-order spectral formulas account for nearly all of this difference. For $p=1.8$ the approximation itself adds to the error, which becomes $3.9\times10^{-5}$ in $n_s$ and $0.047\%$ in $r$. For $\delta=3$, perturbative scalaron decay into a minimally coupled Higgs doublet places the pivot 51.59 e-folds before the end of inflation and gives $n_s=0.9690$ and $r=0.0067$. At fixed $\alpha\mu_0^2=0.006065$ and with the same decay rate prescription, $\delta\simeq8.7$ gives the central $n_s$ value inferred from ACT DR6, Planck, CMB lensing and DESI baryon acoustic oscillations. This comparison uses the published one-dimensional constraint.
item.dc:creator: H. Khodabakhshi, F. Shojai
